chapterNote: Psalm 14 sung again, this time with Elohim in every line where the first edition had the LORD. Same fool, same heart-sentence, same inspection from heaven, same verdict that not even one does good — the indictment Paul cites in Romans 3:10-12 from this poem's first edition, whose wording this recension keeps. What it changes is the middle. Psalm 14's devourers panic because God is with the generation of the righteous; here they panic where there was no fear to panic over, and God scatters the bones of the one who had camped against His people. The last cry is the same longing: if only Israel's salvation would come out of Zion. When God turns His people's captivity, Jacob will rejoice.

1.text: For the choir director. On Mahalath. A maskil of David. The fool has said in his heart, 'There is no God.' They have become corrupt and have done abominable injustice; there is no one who does good.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] upon Mahalath, Maschil [maskil], A Psalm of David. The fool [nabal] has said [amar] in his heart [leb], There is no God [Elohim]. They are corrupt [shachath — ruined], and have done abominable iniquity [avlah — injustice]: there is none that does [asah] good [tov].
1.notes: A second edition of Psalm 14, set on Mahalath (H4257) — a tune-name that also heads Psalm 88 — and called a maskil (H4905). amar nabal be-libbo en Elohim (H5036, H559, H3820, H430): the nabal, the moral fool, says in his heart 'no God' — the same sentence as Psalm 14:1, now in a psalm that never names YHWH at all. hishchitu ve-hitivu avel (H7843, H8581, H5766): they have ruined, they have made abominable, avlah — injustice — where Psalm 14:1 had alilah, deeds. en oseh-tov (H6213, H2896): no doer of good.

2.text: God looked down from heaven on the children of men, to see whether there was anyone with insight, anyone seeking God.
2.amp: God [Elohim] looked down from heaven [shamayim] upon the children [ben] of men [adam], to see [raah] if there [yesh] were any that did understand [sakal — act with insight], that did seek [darash] God [Elohim].
2.notes: Elohim mi-shamayim hishqiph al-bene adam (H430, H8259, H8064, H1121, H120): GOD looked down from heaven upon the children of men — the same inspection as Psalm 14:2, but Elohim where that verse had YHWH. lirot ha-yesh maskil doresh et-Elohim (H7200, H3426, H7919, H1875): to see if there EXISTS one with insight, one seeking God. The search is real; the result is verse 3.

3.text: Every one of them has turned back; together they have gone rotten; there is no one who does good, not even one.
3.amp: Every one of them is gone back; they are altogether [yachad] become filthy [alach]; there is none that does [asah] good [tov], no, not one [echad].
3.notes: kullo sag (H5472): every one of them has turned BACK — sag, not Psalm 14:3's sur, turned aside; yachdav neelachu (H3162, H444): together they have gone rotten — alach, the same rare root as Psalm 14:3 and Job 15:16, a man who drinks injustice like water. en oseh-tov en gam-echad (H6213, H2896, H259): no doer of good — not even ONE. This is the line Romans 3:12 takes up from the poem.

4.text: Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge? They eat up My people as they eat bread; they have not called on God.
4.amp: Have the workers [paal] of iniquity [aven] no knowledge [yada]? who eat up [akal — devour] My people [am] as they eat [akal] bread [lechem]: they have not called [qara] upon God [Elohim].
4.notes: ha-lo yadeu poale aven (H3045, H6466, H205): do the workers of aven not KNOW? okhle ammi akhelu lechem (H398, H5971, H3899): they eat My people the way they eat bread — casually, daily — Elohim lo qarau (H7121, H430): and have not called on God. Psalm 14:4's devourers never called on the LORD; here they do not call on Elohim. The appetite is the same.

5.text: There they were in great dread, where no dread was — for God has scattered the bones of the one who camped against you. You have put them to shame, because God has rejected them.
5.amp: There were they in great fear ['they feared a fear', pachad, the KJV margin], where no fear [pachad] was: for God [Elohim] has scattered the bones [etsem] of him that encamps [chanah] against you: you have put them to shame [bosh], because God [Elohim] has despised [maas — rejected] them.
5.notes: sham pachadu phachad (H6342, H6343): THERE they feared a fear, the margin's literal — and this recension adds where no fear (H6343) was. The terror has no earthly cause; it is God breaking in. ki-Elohim pizzar atsmot chonakh (H430, H6340, H6106, H2583): God has SCATTERED the bones of the one encamped against you — the siege-camp taken apart, not a living army left to bury its dead. hebishothah ki-Elohim me'asam (H954, H3988): you have put them to shame, because God has rejected them. Psalm 14:5-6's 'God is with the generation of the righteous' and 'the LORD is his refuge' are gone; this middle is a battlefield.

6.text: Oh, that Israel's salvation would come out of Zion! When God restores the fortunes of His people, Jacob will rejoice, Israel will be glad.
6.amp: Oh that ['Who will give', natan, the KJV margin] the salvation [yeshuah] of Israel [Yisrael] were come out of Zion [Tsiyyon]! When God [Elohim] brings back [shub] the captivity [shebut] of His people [am], Jacob [Yaaqob] shall rejoice [gil], and Israel [Yisrael] shall be glad [samach].
6.notes: mi yitten mi-Tsiyyon yeshuat Yisrael (H5414, H3444, H3478, H6726): 'who will give', the margin's literal — the Hebrew idiom of longing — salvation for Israel out of Zion. be-shub Elohim shebut ammo (H7725, H430, H7622, H5971): when GOD turns the captivity of His people — Elohim where Psalm 14:7 has YHWH. yagel Yaaqob yismach Yisrael (H1523, H3290, H8055): Jacob will exult, Israel be glad. After the universal verdict and the scattered bones, the psalm still ends looking for a salvation that has to come from God's side.
